output.myth: Aun built his second kite the winter after he cut the string. Ennu the Kite-Wright showed him how to cut the cloth and bend the cane, and Aun sewed it with his own sinew because he trusted no other hands. It was the finest thing he ever made. He carried it to the high cliff and held it up to the wind, meaning to fly it out after the first one and bring it home. Tavo heard him and laughed, and the gale tore the kite from his fingers before he had found the spool. Hesk would not give him more string. She had counted every turn he ever made. So the second kite never left the ground. Aun's sister Sil saw it from the water and wept, and that is why her light is so pale. The kite is still up there, unlit, its tail hanging down into the Leeward. When a child is slow to come in from the wind, we tell them Aun's kite is waiting for someone to hold the spool.
output.verse:
Aun's second kite waits
its tail hangs in the dark south
no hand holds the spool
